lens: public-live website · product rubric · startup/app-release truth

items.premise: The startup brief displayed 70% context used while the live context meter reported roughly 0.5% used, creating false closeout pressure in the single canonical startup surface.
liveEvidence: node scripts/context-meter.mjs --json returned pctUsed below 1 with usedTokens far below the 1,000,000 token limit
docs/STARTUP_BRIEF.md rendered 6,622 / 1,000,000 tok as 70% used before the fix
scripts/render-startup-brief.mjs interpreted pctUsed values below 1 as fractions and multiplied them by 100
items.recipe: Derive the displayed context percentage from usedTokens / limit instead of reinterpreting pctUsed, then re-render and validate the startup brief.

items.premise: The startup brief displayed Context age ?d because CURRENT_STATE.md no longer carries a Last updated header, even though PROJECT_STATUS.lastUpdated is current.
liveEvidence: docs/STARTUP_BRIEF.md displayed Context age ?d before the fix
scripts/render-startup-brief.mjs only parsed CURRENT_STATE.md's optional Last updated header for ctxAge
items.recipe: Fallback ctxAge to PROJECT_STATUS.lastUpdated, then the latest scored SIL header, when CURRENT_STATE lacks a Last updated header.

items.premise: The existing startup-meter freshness gate compared verdict urgency and token limits, but not whether the printed percentage agreed with the printed token counts.
liveEvidence: scripts/check-startup-meter-freshness.mjs parsed verdict and token line but not percent-used
The old guard would pass a CONTINUE brief even when 3,000 / 1,000,000 tok was displayed as 50% used
items.recipe: Parse the displayed percent, compare it to round(usedTokens / limit * 100), and add a self-test fixture for the bad-percent regression.
